extracted.subtask_description: A multi-topic Associated Press newswire page collecting brief reports on wartime policy, military organization and domestic measures (draft rules, prohibition debates, training systems, civil defense). Intended as general-interest news briefs for a broad readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mexican 1943 draft call-up numbers and schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Mexico will call up 183,757 men in the 1943 military draft; the first group of 10,000 will be inducted in January.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported by the National Defense department; used as a planning/scheduling figure for induction and training operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment eligibility and rules for Mexican recruits
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first calling 18-year-olds will be accepted; physical examinations will be severe; no married men are to be enrolled hereafter; barracks are to be rid of the so-called 'Soldaderas' (women who traditionally attached themselves to the Mexican army).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: President Avila Camacho (a professional soldier) emphasized that 'military service must be voluntary' though patriotic feeling makes compulsory service 'absurd' — the policy balances strict physical standards and social restrictions (no married men, removal of women from barracks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mexico–Cuba naval and air support treaty terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Each country agrees to give full support, supply and repair facilities to the other's naval vessels and corresponding privileges to each other's aircraft; provision for patrol of adjacent waters including the Yucatan channel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treaty provisions create reciprocal logistics, repair and patrol privileges to facilitate joint naval/air operations and regional security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prosecution / enforcement standard against anti-Mexico propaganda
rubrics_metrics.description: Government agents preferred charges after investigation of handbills asserting that Americans were not safe in Mexico; possession of such materials was treated as spreading propaganda to break down good relations between Mexico and the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arrests are supported by documentary evidence (papers in possession bearing names/permits); enforcement is aimed at maintaining diplomatic and public-order relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lend‑lease accounting principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep a record to show what was furnished, how it was furnished, who used it and how they used it; communications over vital matters such as lend‑lease should be handled through regular channels (State Department and the embassies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although some suggested canceling accounting because lives lost can't be evaluated in cash, several Senators argued for maintaining records for transparency and postwar settlement; practical handling should go through official diplomatic channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senatorial positions on canceling lend‑lease accounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Views ranged from supporting Venning's idea (settle after the war or treat as gift) to vigorous opposition that U.S. taxpayers should not be forced to 'pay all bills of this war' and that accounting should be retained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflects policy debate: possible legal authority under lend‑lease to 'lend, lease, sell, give or otherwise dispose' versus political/financial responsibility and record-keeping needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Army Specialist Corps appointment criteria (revised policy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Further officers appointed from civil life will be given commissions as specialists in the regular army; appointments will be limited to men with civilian training and experience for a particular position beyond that normally provided at officers' candidate schools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intended to avoid duplication of effort with regular army procurement and training structures; specialists should bring unique civilian skills needed for particular positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transition/abolition policy for Army Specialist Corps
rubrics_metrics.description: The Army Specialist Corps (an auxiliary organization) will be abolished 'in the interest of efficiency'; men now in the corps will be offered commissions in the regular army if qualified and needed; further civilian appointees will be integrated as regular‑army specialists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: War Department decision based on recommendations that 'it was found not advisable to have two uniformed services' doing similar procurement/training work — aimed at eliminating duplication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility/age restrictions for specialist appointments
rubrics_metrics.description: Men under 35 will not be eligible unless in a draft class for physical disability; exceptions may be made only in cases of critical need or if they have prior service as officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised policies tighten eligibility to preserve officer training resources and ensure specialists have required experience; exceptions are narrowly drawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fort Knox Armored Force School 'phase' training system
rubrics_metrics.description: The school switched from conventional class/term operation to a 'phase' system: a new group of students can be started every six days and the department can handle up to eight times as many students; students absent can join the new group at their phase and continue without redoing the whole course.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phase system increases throughput, speeds training, and offers psychological advantages by having students master simple, discrete tasks before progressing to broader subjects; night/shift scheduling (multiple shifts per day, six days a week) further speeds up training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training speed‑up measures (Fort Knox)
rubrics_metrics.description: To increase production of trained men the school initiated multiple shifts per day (examples: first shift early morning to afternoon; second shift afternoon to evening; etc.), allowing continuous use of facilities and higher weekly graduations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industrial-style scheduling and phased instruction borrowed from factory/assembly-line practice to maximize throughput and maintain continuity for students who miss days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition/Lee amendment standard for military establishments
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to make prohibition in and around military establishments a condition for drafting young men aged 18 and 19; sale of liquor on military posts is already banned and some officials proposed extending restrictions (curfews, bans on sales to service personnel).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supporters cited temperance and war-effectiveness arguments; opponents warned it could be a 'stepping stone' to nationwide prohibition and could harm morale or be politically divisive; administrative leaders (e.g., Secretary Stimson) argued the War Department prefers its own internal controls over broad prohibition legislation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local/state restrictions on liquor during wartime
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples cited: Virginia imposed an 11 p.m. curfew on sales of wine and beer for on-premise consumption in areas with swollen populations of war workers and service men; Northern Ireland retailers banned bottled spirits and wine sales to U.S. and British service members after consulting army authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local option elections and wartime emergency measures may be used to restrict alcohol sales where population shifts or security concerns justify them.

rubrics_metrics.name: WPB diversion of distillery output policy
rubrics_metrics.description: War Production Board diverted the entire output of the country's distilleries into industrial alcohol; WPB might later permit distilleries to revert to liquor production for limited periods (e.g., two months each year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy reflects priority of war production needs over civilian liquor supply; temperance groups urged further action (redistillation of stocks, nationwide prohibition) as wartime necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil Defense air-raid wardens staffing and training recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Call for replacement of air‑raid wardens lost to military service and industry with at least 50% women among new wardens; re-establish statewide school system for war-control; recruit, train and drill wardens; provide instruction in wartime traffic control and other phases of civilian defense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schools should teach function, equipment and other details of state/local transportation programs, purposes/methods/agencies of emergency traffic control, and the civilian war service program; 'block plan' organization recommended for complete household coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of a 'normal' (customary) bonus for tax/business purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'normal' bonus is one customarily given in the past (e.g., a regular weekly pay bonus); if bonuses were given in good years only but the current year is a good year, they are still considered customary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Q&A indicates that recurring historical practice determines whether a bonus is 'normal'; whether an incentive plan counts if bonuses were never paid is left open by the excerpt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment projection and workforce mobilization expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Employment reported at an all-time peak with projections that at least another 4,500,000 workers — including 3,000,000 women — will be needed next year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as planning guidance for labor mobilization and recruitment efforts during wartime; supports policy measures to broaden workforce participation.
